beats.caption: Memory makers sell chips by the pallet and by the lot
beats.text: DRAM and NAND come off the fab as trays of packaged chips. A few makers supply nearly all of it, and they sell through two channels with two different prices.

beats.caption: Contract price: what big buyers negotiate
beats.text: Hyperscalers, PC and phone makers buy huge volumes on agreements that reset monthly or quarterly. That negotiated per-chip price is the contract price, and it covers most of the industry's revenue.

beats.caption: Spot price: small lots that trade every day
beats.text: Brokers and smaller buyers trade leftover chips daily. The spot price reacts quickly to shortages or gluts, so it is noisy.

beats.caption: Spot moves first; contract follows in steps
beats.text: When spot runs above contract, buyers expect the next negotiation to rise, and vice versa. Contract prices move in quarterly steps that trail the spot trend, which makes spot a leading indicator.

beats.caption: Contract trends drive memory makers' earnings
beats.text: A 10-20% quarterly move in contract price flows almost straight into gross margin, since fab costs are mostly fixed. That is why analysts track it on every earnings call. Related: Micron (MU), Samsung (005930.KS), SK hynix (000660.KS), Sandisk (SNDK).
